Three public hearings have been held regarding the CDBG program. The first hearing was on the citizen participation plan; the second was held December 12 for the purpose of designating Comprehensive Neighborhood Revitalization Ar is (CNRA). A third hearing on January 24 was the final public hearing on the CDBG program for the fourth year, at which the City Council firmly adopted the CDBG plan in concept.
The CDBG Steering Committee prepared its recommendation through a comprehensive citizen participation process. In a series of nine meetings, the Steering Committee reviewed a recommendation from the City Administration and thirty-nine (39) citizen proposals for CDBG funding. This process included an all-day meeting on December 10 to hear the citizen proposals. For the first time in the CDBG planning process, consultant assistance was provided for citizens wishing to submit proposals.
The Committee's recommendation included a three-year program for the fourth, fifth and sixth years of CDBG funding. The portion of the plan covering the fourth CDBG year will be included in the 1978 application for funding. Projects were evaluated based on the proposed regulations for the CDBG program. Final regulations will not be published until the end of January, 1978.
The recommended plan continues the strategy of improving neighborhoods by funding housing rehabilitation and needed capital improvements. A program is proposed in each of the seven Concentrated Neighborhood Revitalization Areas designated by the City Council on December 12, 1977. Several citywide projects, including facilities for the handicapped, the Housing Service Center, and the Redevelopment Program, are also proposed.
Housing Assistance Plan
In addition to the program recommendation, the CDBG Application contains a Housing Assistance Plan (HAP), identifying San Jose's housing conditions, needs and goals.
The HAP covers the fourth program year (1978-1979) and the three-year period of 1978-1981, as required by HUD. The plan is essentially the same as the plan adopted by City Council last year. The important differences between the 1977-1978 HAP and 1978-1981 are as follows:
1. The estimate of households needing housing assistance was updated to reflect the increased population over the past year. It was projected that 31,542 lower-income households would have needed housing assistance in January, 1978 (compared with 29,021 in January, 1977). However, the net increase in assisted units in 1977 (1090 units) was subtracted from 31,542, resulting in 30,452 lower-income households needing housing assistance in January, 1978.
